newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Mar 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Mar 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:

* President Clinton said he and his senior staff were not told that the Federal Bureau of Investigation had warned the White House National Security Council last year about possible efforts by China to buy political influence through contributions to Congressional campaigns.

* Federal and New York law officials are expected to tell Congress today that a Treasury Department order imposing a $750-per-transaction limit on remittance shops suspected of wiring drug money has sharply cut money laundering.
* Vietnam has agreed to repay the United States millions of dollars in debts incurred by the former South Vietnam for roads, power stations and grain shipments during the Vietnam War.

* Allies of New York Governor George Pataki are opposing his plan to enact sweeping welfare changes that include mandatory drug testing of adult recipients and the reduction of cash benefits for many poor families.

* Some consultants and members of Congress say recent disclosures about Vice President Al Gore's involvement in last year's political fund-raising efforts have clouded his prospects for winning the presidential nomination in 2000.
* Zaire's five-month old armed rebellion against President Mobutu Sese Seko is also an assault on Zaire's parliament, which has not produced any new laws for months.
* Russia remains a highly sexist society in which wives of newly rich businessmen find that money and privilege are shadowed by isolation, anxiety and boredom.
